regulatedProfessionsBanner.title: Regulated Professions
regulatedProfessionsBanner.text:
For regulated professions, the professional qualification is particularly protected. If you studied a regulated profession, you will need to have it recognized in Germany to practice your profession. Regulated professions in Germany include, among others, doctors and the entire healthcare sector, teachers, and more. 

What happens if your qualification is not fully recognized? 

In this case, the competent authority will establish a compensatory measure with which you can compensate for the fundamental differences. If you successfully complete the compensatory measure, equivalency will be declared.
regulatedProfessionsBanner.text2: If you studied a non-regulated profession in a non-EU country, a requirement for applying for an employment visa in Germany or a job-seeking visa is the recognition of your academic qualifications in Germany.

banner.title: Recognition of Professional Qualifications in Germany
banner.subtitle: If you have studied a university profession for 4 to 5 years and want to have your university studies recognized in Germany, you can consult with us to submit your application to the competent authority based on your profession.

homologationPage.pageText: Working as a healthcare professional in Germany will bring great rewards: attractive salaries, security, and stability for you and your family, as well as the possibility of continuous professional growth. Doctors, specialists, and cutting-edge facilities make the German healthcare system one of the best in the world, and you can be part of it. Since medicine is a regulated profession in Germany, it is necessary to have your degree recognized to practice it within the country. We guide you every step of the way and handle the paperwork so you can obtain the state authorization to practice and achieve your goal of getting a job in Germany. As for the language, you can learn it alongside the homologation process with us until you reach a B2 level in German, while we take care of the documentation and bureaucracy in Germany. Before you pack your bags, we prepare your paperwork so you can travel with confidence and firm steps towards your future.

homologationPage.faqAnswer1: The recognition of your professional qualifications means that your foreign qualifications are comparable to a German profession. For example, if you have a degree as an electronics technician, your skills and knowledge will be comparable to those of someone with the title Elektrotechniker in Germany.
homologationPage.faqAnswer2: Also known as regulated professions, where professionals must have certain specific or technical qualifications to practice in Germany. For example, doctors, teachers, or architects. If you obtain a partial recognition of your qualifications but need to compensate for technical, practical, and language deficiencies to achieve your approval, you can apply for a residence permit to complete your recognition as part of a qualification measure (Qualifizierungsmaßnahme). For this, you generally need A2-level German and the ability to finance your stay in Germany.
homologationPage.faqQuestion3: Is there an age limit to work in Germany?
homologationPage.faqAnswer3: Age is not a problem; there is no age limit.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.answer1: The recognition of your professional qualifications means that your foreign qualifications are comparable to a German profession. For example, if you have a degree as an electronics technician, your skills and knowledge will be comparable to those who obtain the Elektrotechniker title in Germany.
faq.answer2: These are also called regulated professions, where professionals must have certain specific or technical qualifications to practice the profession in Germany. For example, Doctors, Teachers, or Architects. If you receive partial recognition of your qualifications but must compensate for technical, practical, and language deficiencies to reach full approval, you can apply for a residence permit to complete your recognition as part of a qualification measure (Qualifizierungsmaßnahme). To do this, you generally need an A2 level of German and the ability to finance your stay in Germany.
faq.question3: Is there an age limit to work in Germany?
faq.answer3: Age is not an issue, there is no age limit.
